topics.title: NoSQL Basics
topics.description: NoSQL (Not Only SQL) databases are designed to handle large volumes of unstructured or semi-structured data, offering more flexibility and scalability than traditional relational databases. They emerged to address the limitations of relational databases for web-scale applications and big data environments.

coreCharacteristics.description: Schema-less or dynamic schema: no predefined schema is required, so data structures can evolve over time. Adaptive data models accommodate structural changes without system downtime.
Horizontal scalability: scale out by adding more servers or nodes. A distributed architecture spreads data across multiple nodes for better performance and fault tolerance.
Optimized for specific data models: each NoSQL type excels at different access patterns, and most are tuned for high read or high write throughput depending on their type.

topics.title: CAP & BASE
topics.description: The CAP theorem states that a distributed database system can only guarantee two of these three properties simultaneously. In contrast to the ACID properties of traditional relational databases, NoSQL often follows BASE instead.

capProperties.name: Consistency
capProperties.description: All nodes see the same data at the same time.

capProperties.name: Availability
capProperties.description: Every request receives a response, without a guarantee that it contains the most recent data.

capProperties.name: Partition Tolerance
capProperties.description: The system continues to operate despite network partitions.

topics.capTradeoff: Most NoSQL databases prioritize availability and partition tolerance over strong consistency, often implementing eventual consistency models.

baseProperties.name: Soft State
baseProperties.description: The state of the system may change over time.

baseProperties.name: Eventual Consistency
baseProperties.description: The system will eventually become consistent.

topics.title: Document Stores
topics.description: Store data as documents, usually JSON, BSON, or XML.
characteristics: Documents are self-contained with all necessary information
Flexible schema allows for nested data
Good for content management, user profiles, and catalog data

topics.title: Key-Value Stores
topics.description: The simplest NoSQL type, storing data as key-value pairs.

topics.title: Column-Family Stores
topics.description: Store data in column families, which are groups of related data.
characteristics: Optimized for queries over large datasets
Highly scalable for writes and reads
Schema flexibility at the column level

topics.title: Graph Databases
topics.description: Store data in nodes and edges representing relationships.

topics.title: NoSQL vs SQL
topics.description: How NoSQL and relational databases compare across the dimensions interviewers ask about.

topics.title: Consistency Models
topics.description: NoSQL databases offer a spectrum of consistency guarantees rather than a single one.

models.name: Eventual Consistency
models.description: Data updates propagate through the system eventually. Different nodes may return different values during the propagation period. Improves availability and performance at the cost of immediate consistency.

models.name: Strong Consistency
models.description: All reads receive the most recent write or an error. Ensures data integrity but may reduce availability during network partitions.

models.name: Causal Consistency
models.description: Operations that are causally related appear in the same order to all processes. Unrelated operations may be observed in different orders.

topics.title: Data Modeling
topics.description: NoSQL modeling optimizes for access patterns rather than normal forms.
denormalization: Redundant data is often intentionally stored across documents or entities
Reduces join operations by embedding related data
Improves read performance at the cost of write complexity

embeddingVsReferencing.description: Including related data within a document.

topics.title: Sharding
topics.description: Sharding is the horizontal partitioning of data across multiple nodes.
fundamentals: Horizontal partitioning of data across multiple nodes
Common sharding keys: user ID, geographic location, time range

types.description: Divides data based on ranges of values.
Uses a hash function to determine data placement.
Maintains a lookup table for shard locations.

topics.title: Patterns
topics.description: Common implementation patterns that put NoSQL stores to work in real architectures.

implementationPatterns.description: Using different database types for different data requirements. For example Redis for caching, MongoDB for user profiles, and Neo4j for relationships.
Separating read and write operations, using different data models or even different databases for reads versus writes.
Storing changes to application state as a sequence of events, often combined with NoSQL for event storage and processing.

microservices: Each service can use the most appropriate database type
Enables polyglot persistence (using multiple database technologies)

topics.title: Security & Ops
topics.description: Security, performance tuning, and monitoring concerns specific to NoSQL deployments.

security.name: Authentication and Authorization
security.description: Many NoSQL databases have limited built-in security features, so application-level security controls should be implemented.

security.name: Data Encryption
security.description: Encryption at rest and in transit, plus field-level encryption for sensitive data.

security.name: Injection Prevention
security.description: NoSQL injection vulnerabilities differ from SQL injection, but input validation and parameterized queries remain important.

performanceOptimization.name: Indexing
performanceOptimization.description: Create indexes appropriate to the NoSQL type and understand the performance impact of each index.

performanceOptimization.name: Query Optimization
performanceOptimization.description: Design queries to leverage database strengths and avoid operations that cause full collection scans.

performanceOptimization.name: Caching Strategies
performanceOptimization.description: Implement application-level caching and use dedicated caching layers such as Redis.

managementTools: Monitoring solutions such as Prometheus and Grafana

topics.title: Interview Questions
topics.description: The ten questions this topic is most often tested on.

questions.question: What is NoSQL and why would you choose it over a relational database?
answer: NoSQL offers schema flexibility, horizontal scalability, and specialized data models for specific use cases.
Choose NoSQL when dealing with large volumes of unstructured or semi-structured data, requiring high write throughput, or needing horizontal scalability.

questions.question: Explain the CAP theorem and how it applies to different NoSQL databases.
answer: Most document stores prioritize CP (MongoDB in certain configurations) or AP (CouchDB)
Key-value stores often prioritize AP (Redis, DynamoDB)
Column-family stores typically favor AP (Cassandra) or CP (HBase)

questions.question: How would you handle ACID transactions in a NoSQL environment?
answer: Some NoSQL databases support limited transactions, for example MongoDB
Implement eventual consistency patterns like compensating transactions
Consider using multiple database technologies for different parts of the application

questions.question: Describe the differences between MongoDB and Cassandra in terms of data model, scaling, and use cases.
answer: MongoDB: document-oriented, master-slave architecture, flexible querying
Cassandra: column-family, masterless architecture, optimized for high write throughput

questions.question: How would you design a NoSQL schema for a social media application?
answer: Consider embedding versus referencing for user relationships
Use denormalization for frequently accessed data
Possibly combine different NoSQL types: graph for connections, document for profiles

questions.question: What are the main challenges of migrating from SQL to NoSQL?
answer: Redesigning data models and schemas
Rewriting queries and transactions
Ensuring data consistency during and after migration
Retraining development and operations teams

questions.question: Explain sharding and partitioning in NoSQL databases.
answer: Sharding is distributing data across multiple servers based on a shard key
Effective partitioning depends on workload analysis and access patterns
Requires careful key selection to avoid hotspots

questions.question: How does NoSQL handle data consistency in a distributed environment?
answer: Most implement eventual consistency models
Some offer stronger consistency guarantees with performance tradeoffs
Application design must account for consistency requirements

questions.question: Compare Redis and MongoDB for caching use cases.
answer: Redis: in-memory, faster, simpler data structures, built-in TTL
MongoDB: more flexible querying, persistent by default, better for complex documents

questions.question: What monitoring metrics are important for NoSQL databases?
answer: Read and write latency and throughput
Cache hit rates
Node health in distributed systems
Index usage statistics
